speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis (Cradle Cap).
The history of a red, scaly rash appearing in cold weather on an infant with a family history of psoriasis is classic for this condition. Given the chronic nature and specific triggers, I will monitor progress, but no further immediate tests are required unless the rash becomes infected or fails to respond to standard care.
